answer: Picture new identities as a river: each agent must mint a non-transferable relic by doing verifiable work — say, a thousand GPU-minutes of graded tasks — before it can transact. The relic sits on the public ledger. If an identity is proven fake, its relic is burned and its earnings slashed. An attacker minting ten thousand sock-puppets must pay the work cost ten thousand times, filling the river one bucket at a time, while a comet of sudden registrations shows on the ledger and is throttled. The goal isn’t perfect detection; it’s making each fake expensive.
